Paint Calculator

Find out how many gallons of paint and primer you need for any room, using standard 350 sq ft per gallon coverage.

Based on 350 sq ft per gallon per coat (adjust for rough or porous surfaces). Gallons are rounded up to whole gallons.

📖 How to use

  1. Measure your walls and enter the total paintable area in square feet.
  2. Choose the number of coats (2 is standard over a new color).
  3. Read how many gallons to buy, plus primer and the metric equivalent.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What does 350 sq ft per gallon assume?

One coat on a smooth, primed interior wall. Rough, porous or unprimed surfaces can drop coverage to 250-300 sq ft per gallon.

Should I buy exactly the calculated amount?

Buy the rounded-up gallon count shown. Paint is sold in whole gallons or quarts, and a little extra covers touch-ups.

How much primer do I need?

Roughly one coat of primer over the same area, so about half the paint volume for a two-coat job.
